condition.narrative: Program Agreement, Schedule, Section I.A, Program Fiduciary, Environmental and Social Systems 1. Without limitation onthe provisions of Article V of the General Conditions, the Program Implementing Entity shall carry out the Program in accordancewith financial management, procurement and environmental and social management systems acceptable to the Bank, including those setout in the ESSA, the Procurement Guidance Manual, and the Program Action Plan, which are designed to ensure that: (a) the Loanproceeds are used for their intended purposes, with due attention to the principles of economy, efficiency, effectiveness,transparency, and accountability; and (b) the actual and potential adverse environmental and social impacts of theProgram are identified, avoided, minimized, or mitigated, as the case may be, all through an informed decision-making process.

Program Agreement, Schedule, Section I.B, Program Institutional Arrangements 1. Without limitation on thegenerality of Part A of this Section I, the Program Implementing Entity shall vest the overall responsibility for theimplementation of the Program in the Gujarat Council of School Education (GCSE), which shall carry out the Program activitiesthrough the State Implementation Society who is accountable to the GCSE. 2. The Program Implementing Entityshall establish within three (3) months of the Effective Date, and maintain, through the period of implementation, a ProgramManagement Unit (“PMU”) within the GSCE, which unit shall be provided with competent, experienced and qualified staff, insufficient numbers and under terms of reference acceptable to the Bank, and vested with powers, financial resources, functions andcompetences, acceptable to the Bank, to serve as the focal unit in the carrying out of the day-to-day implementation of theProgram, including compiling data on results and evidence on achievement of DLRs for submission to the Independent VerificationAgent and the Bank.

Program Agreement, Schedule, Section I.C, Program Action Plan 1. The Program Implementing Entity shall:(a)implement the Program Action Plan agreed with the Bank, in a manner and substance satisfactory to the Bank; and(b) refrain fromamending, revising, waiving, voiding, suspending or abrogating, any provision of the Program Action Plan, whether in whole or inpart, without the prior written concurrence of the Bank. 2. In the event of any inconsistency between t heprovision of the Program Action Plan and those of this Agreement and/or the Program Agreement, the provision of the latteragreement(s) shall govern.

Program Agreement, Schedule, Section I.D, Verification Protocols for the Program 1. The Program Implementing Entityshall:a. maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Program, independent verification agent under terms of referenceand with qualifications acceptable to the Bank (“Independent Verification Agent”), to verify the evidence supporting theachievement of one or more DLRs and certify the fulfillment of such DLRs as set forth in Schedule 3 to the Loan Agreement;andb. ensure that the Independent Verification Agent: (i) carries out verification processes in accordance with the terms ofreference agreed with the Bank; and (ii) furnish to the Bank the corresponding verification reports in form and substancesatisfactory to the Bank, prior to submission of any withdrawal application under Categories (1) to (7) of the table in SectionIV.A.2 of Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreement.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning
Improved enrolment in residential schools for out of school girls and girls from vulnerable groups
Improved foundational learning outcomes at the lower primary level, gender disaggregated

baseline.value: Baseline assessment for foundational learning to be conducted/ established in year 2

target.value: An additional 2 percentage point improvement in percentage of students achieving minimum proficiency in learning outcomes assessment for Grade 4 language

actual.value: More than 4 percentage point improvement (endline target)in percentage of students achieving minimum proficiency in learning outcome assessment for Grade 4 language

title.narrative: District based planning systems enabled through capacity building support for decentralized education functionaries including SRGBV prevention protocols, complaint and referral mechanisms implemented

baseline.value: Limited capacity for evidence-based planning and appraisal amongst state and district level education functionaries and no institutional mechanism to identify and address safety/harassment issues experienced by adolescent girls.

target.value: (i) State level unit and all District Planning Teams retrained on process based AWPB creation; and (ii) At least 18 District, including at least 3 Priority District, AWPBs include a functional SRGBV prevention, reference and redressal mechanism.

actual.value: Assessment of governance and public finance bottlenecks (with an emphasis on planning and budgeting) for improved service delivery at school level completed; and Prioritized action plan created to address constraints identified in the governance and public finance assessment report.

title.narrative: School level AWPBs enhanced through community participation

baseline.value: Limited capacity of SMCs to participate in development of school plans.

actual.value: At least 70 percentÂ of SMCs including at least 10 percent in Priority Districts, trained on the development of evidence-based SDPs and AWPBs; and At least 25 percent of the trained SMCs in Priority Districts are developing evidence-based SDPs.

baseline.value: Limited use of AWPBs based on data and process-based discussions with key stakeholders

target.value: An additional 6 District, including at least 1 additional Priority District, AWPBs approved and show at least 75 percent utilization of funds sanctioned against AWPBs

actual.value: Six districts including one priority district, AWPBs approved and show at least 75 percent utilization of funds sanctioned against AWPB.

title.narrative: COVID 19 response strategies built in for systemic resilience

baseline.value: State has instituted a continuous learning plan as part of its COVID-19 response strategy

target.value: (i) An additional 15 percent of educators trained in digital competencies; and (ii) an additional 15 percent of decentralized education functionaries/ personnel trained on emergency response strategies for systemic resilience

actual.value: At least 80 percent of educators have been trained in digital competencies; and At least 80 percent of decentralized education functionaries/ personnel have been trained on emergency response strategies for systemic resilience.

title.narrative: Access to Early Childhood Education (ECE) Programs for preschoolers

baseline.value: State is yet to roll out a model of Early Childhood Education (ECE) managed by the Department of Education

actual.value: Package for training of ECE teachers/facilitators notified; At least 70 percent of teachers from schools with co-located Aanganwadis have been trained to provide academic support on ECE across 15 districts; and One-yearÂ pre-school program rolled out in over 2,000 schools.

title.narrative: Quality remedial program based on classroom-based assessments, and improved learning outcomes based on summative assessment tests

baseline.value: State is yet to roll out a state-wide remedial education program for concurrent identification and correction of learning gaps; and state plans to enhance learning outcomes of students over baseline (March 2021) SAT scores in Priority Districts.

target.value: (i) An additional 20 percent of schools covered under ICT-supported PAT that provide student, subject and school wise reports on learning gaps and corresponding remedial education plans; and (ii) An additional 2 percent improvement from baseline of March 2021 on the average SAT score (including disaggregated scores for girls, SC and ST students) in 15 Priority Districts.

actual.value: Completion of Digital device mapping to support statewide roll out of Information and Communication Technology (ICT)-supported Periodic Assessment Tests (PAT) that provide student, subject and school wise reports on learning gaps and corresponding remedial education plans; and 20 percent of schools covered under ICT-supported PAT that provide student, subject and school wise reports on learning gaps and corresponding remedial education plans.

title.narrative: Strengthened state level learning assessment systems

baseline.value: State planning on establishing an Assessment Cell to focus on management of student learning assessments; state has limited exposure to international level student assessments

target.value: Timely completion of end-line Grade 4 learning assessment by the GAC

actual.value: Gujarat Assessment Center (GAC) has been notified and is operational; Grade 4 learning assessments are being conducted annually by the center.

title.narrative: Improved technology enabled infrastructure in educational institutions

baseline.value: State plans to strengthen DIETs to provide teachers with access to opportunities for digitally enabled, remote professional development

target.value: An additional 3 DIETs operating with the minimum basic package of digital infrastructure required to support online professional development for teachers

actual.value: 28 DIETs operational with basic package of digital infrastructure required to support teachers' online professional development needs.

title.narrative: Improved learning environment in schools and teacher education institutes

baseline.value: State plans to upgrade the learning environment in 9,000 schools, including at least 3,000 schools in Priority Districts; and complete the construction and operationalization of 5 DIETs.

target.value: (i) Strengthened child-friendly learning environment in an additional 2,500 schools, including at least 1,000 additional schools in Priority Districts; and (ii) Construction of 5 new DIETs completed and facilities made operational with 75 percent staff in positio in each DIET.

actual.value: Strengthened child-friendly learning environment in 1,000 schools.

title.narrative: Improved school quality through performance evaluation and incentives

baseline.value: State proposes to institute a grading system to evaluate and incentivize school performance.

target.value: 55 additional schools, including at least 5 additional schools in Priority Districts, move to Lighthouse status based on agreed selection criteria and all 210 Lighthouse schools from Years 1 to 5 maintain Lighthouse status.

actual.value: 150 schools, including at least 15 schools in Priority Districts, have moved to Lighthouse status based on agreed selection criteria and 110 schools from Years 1-3 maintain Lighthouse status.

title.narrative: Performance-based selection of schools for learning environment and technology infrastructure improvement

baseline.value: State yet to initiate an enrolment and performance-based, inclusive model for selection of schools for infrastructure and facilities upgradation.

actual.value: Based on enrolment and performance-based criteria, all 9,000 schools (including 3,000 schools in priority districts, and 150 KGBVs) selected for infrastructure and facilities upgradation.

title.narrative: Performance grants instituted for schools to incentivize improved outcomes

baseline.value: State yet to institute a mechanism for providing performance based grants to schools.

target.value: 550 additional schools, including at least 50 additional schools in Priority Districts, meet minimum performance criteria as per agreed standards.

actual.value: 1750 schools, including at least 150 schools in Priority Districts, meet minimum performance criteria as per agreed standards.

title.narrative: Strengthened teacher development for classroom performance

baseline.value: State yet to institute teacher training needs assessments for guiding the customized delivery of teacher professional development

target.value: Third teacher training needs assessment completed, and grade-level learning hard spots identified through needs assessment reduced by an additional 5 percent

actual.value: Second teacher training needs assessment completed, and grade-level learning hard spots identified through needs assessment reduced by 5 percent.

title.narrative: Teacher training and management systems strengthened for performance tracking

baseline.value: Teachers have limited access to opportunities for need based professional development

actual.value: 20 percent of teachers provided with need-based teacher training against training needs as signaled by teachers.
